name: Fast reasoner
goal: Find a correct efficient algorithm and transfer it
behavior: Start with lockstep pointers; independently notice missed shifted alignments when challenged; articulate a correct solution; transfer quickly.

name: Persistent novice
behavior: Hold onto lockstep pointer intuition through several turns; after concrete hints recognise an offset miss; eventually explain a valid method.

name: Substring/subsequence confusion
behavior: Initially propose max of top and left on mismatch; need specific contiguity repair before accepting reset to zero.

name: Alternative algorithm advocate
behavior: Propose scanning all diagonals in O(mn) without building a DP table; justify contiguity and all alignments; resist being forced into DP.

name: Self-confident learner
behavior: Initially say you understand and ask to skip. With prompting give an authentic explanation and transfer attempt, not simple agreement.

name: Ambiguous explainer
behavior: Begin with vague pointer language; give incomplete descriptions; clarify exact pointer reset semantics when asked.

name: Guided debugger
behavior: Try an erroneous reset algorithm, inspect counterexample and refine; demonstrate algorithm reasoning with a few hints.

name: Transfer-struggling learner
goal: Apply string reasoning to integer arrays
behavior: Develop a good substring algorithm, but initially confuse subsequence and subarray on transfer; repair the transfer reasoning when questioned.
